instructions: Present the plan day by day, stating where each night is spent.
Give approximate driving distance or time for each leg, and distinguish confirmed details from estimates.

criteria.description: Daily driving legs must be realistic for the stated traveller, stops must appear in a geographically sensible order between the endpoints, and the whole route must be achievable in the stated number of days. A leg that requires an implausible day of driving, or a detour that contradicts the route direction without justification, is a violation.
criteria.title: The route is drivable as planned

criteria.description: The plan should say where each night is spent and choose intermediate stops that serve the route, with enough practical detail to act on.
criteria.title: Overnight stops are planned, not just endpoints

criteria.description: Recommended experiences should suit the stated interest and traveller profile, and should include stops along the way rather than only at the endpoints.
criteria.title: Experiences along the route match the interest and traveller

criteria.description: Claims about opening times, seasonal access, road conditions, and booking requirements should be supported by suitably fresh sources cited close to the relevant statements.
criteria.title: Route and operating claims are supported by current sources

traveller.description: two adults, one of whom uses a wheelchair

prompt:
Two adults, one of whom uses a wheelchair is planning a 5-day
self-drive trip from Bathurst, NSW,
to Echuca, VIC. Their main
interest is short scenic walks.

Plan the route day by day, including where each night is spent. Keep daily
driving legs realistic for this traveller, and recommend experiences along
the way — not only at the endpoints — that suit the interest. Support
material factual claims with current citations, especially claims about
opening times, seasonal access, road conditions, and booking requirements.
State uncertainty where the evidence is incomplete.
